newsitem.title: UK: IPE natgas hits record volume, prices firm.
newsitem.headline: IPE natgas hits record volume, prices firm.

text.p: IPE natural gas futures easily set a new volume record on Thursday as 960 lots traded, most at higher prices, and well above the previous record total of 575 lots.
And the month as a whole has also set a new record, with 5115 lots traded in July, up from the previous record of 4425 lots done in April.
The winter strip from October to March saw the bulk of the trade, with 835 lots done then. In Q1 alone 685 lots were done.

Based on the last deals done in each of the months which make up Q1, the quarter was worth 17.22 pence a therm by the close. This was lower than at the close of the morning session, but January and February reached contract highs, both trading at 18.70 pence for the last time.
There were also 50 lots done in May, and 75 lots done in two trades in August 98 on its first day.

A futures broker said he was surprised by the volume of trade but added he did not know of any production problems or other events which might have contributed to the large volume. Most of the deals, 855 lots, were done in the first 45 minutes after the contract opened.
He added that the anonymity offered by the contract was one of the main reasons for its increasing popularity.

The contract, which has seen extremely variable volumes of trade since its launch at the end of January, has now enjoyed three weeks of relatively high volumes and some feel that it appears to be reaching a degree of consistency.

A physical trader said there were indications the forward curve was tightening and added that "there seems to be a slight squeeze out there," and he was not surprised to see prices rise on the futures market as a result.
At least six different counterparties were seen involved in the trade.
An IPE spokeswoman warned that despite the encouragement of the last three weeks, volumes may drop going into August when gas market activity is traditionally at its weakest.
